editorial:
Imagine being only eight years old and seeing something so scary that it changes how you act every single day. That is exactly what happens to little Josephine. After she sees a violent attack, she doesn't just get sad; she starts acting out and getting aggressive to keep herself safe. You get to see her family fall apart as her parents fight over how to help her while trying to find the person responsible. The vibe is heavy and emotional, making you feel the stress of a home where no one knows how to fix the pain.

The acting is the best part here because the child actor makes you believe every single scream and tantrum. While the middle part of the story drags a bit, the payoff is worth it. If you like stories that pull at your heartstrings and keep you guessing about the crime, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Josephine finally tells the police who committed the crime. It turns out the attacker was a trusted family friend who had been visiting their home. Once he is arrested, the tension in the house finally breaks. The movie ends with Josephine starting therapy and hugging her parents, showing that while they are still hurting, they are finally on the path to healing and feeling safe again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gripping family dramas and crime mysteries.
